In his later years, he recited the *Lotus Sūtra* daily and styled himself the "Patriarch of Tiantai. He also devoted himself to the study of Chan. Yang Shigu once sent him a poem which said:
"Master Nian sits in emaciated meditation, guarding his mind like a tiger in captivity. His letter to Zhao Heshun (Zihuo) states: "I..."
Śākyamuni Buddha and Amitābha Buddha established this single gate of the Pure Land outside of the infinite and boundless Dharma-gates.
Śākyamuni serves as its guest; Amitābha presides over it as its host. Śākyamuni administers medicine for the sick;
Amitābha enables one to live without death throughout their entire life. Śākyamuni’s land is like a transient inn; Amitābha’s...
The land of [Amitābha] is like one's own native village; looking from Western India toward the Land of Peace and Bliss is the same as looking from China toward the Land of Peace and Bliss.
(From *Wangguan wen*)
Wang Shao, courtesy name Zichun, served as the Prefect of Hongzhou. He invited Chan Master Huitang to inquire about the Way, and they reached a silent accord.
Consequently, Wang composed a verse on seizing the opportune moment, which said: "By day I forgot to eat, by night I forgot to sleep;
Holding the dragon pearl, I wished to ascend to heaven. Yet I cast it all down within my own body; Its four corners touch the ground, perfectly round. Master Tang deeply approved of this.

Liu Yuancheng, whose courtesy name was Qizhi, was a native of Wei. Having passed the jinshi examination, he did not seek an official appointment but instead followed Sima Guang to study, inquiring about the essentials of exhausting one's heart-mind and practicing integrity in conduct.
Sima Guang instructed him with the principle of sincerity (*cheng*), beginning by ordering him to refrain from speaking falsely.

Serving in the offices of Censor-in-Chief and Remonstrance, he was upright and resolute in his discussions of state affairs; the powerful and influential held their hands in awe, referring to him as the "Tiger of the Hall.
Loyal, filial, and upright, he never displayed a look of indolence while at home. He once said, "I wish to be a complete man of the Yuanyou era, so that I may meet Sima Guang in the underworld.
The Master once said to his disciple Yongqing, "The Buddha-dharma reached its decline during the Liang dynasty."
Everyone recognizes and clings to form and appearance (*rūpa-lakṣaṇa*). As for Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, though he was the sovereign of men, he did not know how to govern his people;
he brought the world to chaos. How could this have been the intention of the Buddha? When Bodhidharma came from the West, his teaching was not to recognize form and appearance.

Those of superior capacity and keen intelligence mostly delighted in his teaching, and thus it spread. Although my banishment to the south has meant that I have, in my daily life, applied myself to the most urgent matters of our own Confucian tradition...
One gains strength in this matter; yet it cannot be said that one does not gain strength in other matters.

Is there anything in the world greater than birth and death? Yet this matter alone is of a single flavor. If one understands birth and death and possesses a point of view regarding them, then honor and disgrace, fortune and misfortune, will be regarded lightly.
Furthermore, I once took the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and showed it to Yongqing, saying: "The Great Being Avalokiteśvara... [He] perfumed...
Hearing is perfected as hearing. The six faculties are dissolved and restored, becoming identical with the faculty of hearing.
This enables sentient beings who are about to be harmed so that their weapons are like slicing through water or blowing across light; in nature, they possess no movement.
For while one may slice water or blow across light, the natures of water and light do not waver. Thus, even when encountering harm, my nature remains profoundly still. This is Avalokiteśvara.

This is the power of fearlessness. It is also said: when the nature of sound is completely dissolved and the faculties of hearing and seeing turn back into themselves, one leaves behind all sensory dust and delusions.
This enables sentient beings such that they cannot be bound by shackles and fetters; it is said that once a person attains the power of fearlessness, shackles and fetters can no longer cause harm.
Thus, when the Patriarch faced execution, he said: "To meet a white blade with my head is just like cutting through the spring breeze."
He further called Yongqing and entrusted him, saying: "My friend, you may explain this principle to others, so that future generations do not come to slander the Buddha.
(Fahxi zhi, Scroll 3)
*Fǎxīzhì* (The Record of Dharma Joy), Volume Four.
Compiled by the Daoist Bīnglián (Lotus in Ice), Xià Shùfāng;
reviewed by the Layman Jiùdǒu, Fēng Dìng.
Hu Kanghou, whose courtesy name was Kanghou, was a native of Chong’an. He passed the jinshi examination during the Shaosheng era and served in various high-ranking offices.

Xie Liangze once praised him, saying he was like the majestic pine and cypress that stand out alone while all other plants wither and die amidst the bitter cold and heavy snow of winter. His writings include...

There was a commentary on the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, for which he was eventually posthumously titled Wending (Wen-ding). For a long time, Master Gong relied upon Chan Master Xiu of Shangfeng, through whom he attained the meaning beyond words.
During the Chongning era, while passing by Yaoshan, a Zen practitioner raised the story of Nanquan killing the cat to question him.

Master Gong replied with this verse: "In hand, the pivot of life and death, encompassing heaven and earth; To deploy them freely or restrict them depends on the occasion. The jade hall, the rabbit, and the horse..."
"Not a dragon or an elephant; its great function is majestic and grand, yet entirely unknown. He also sent a poem to Shangfeng, which says: "Mount Zhurong is the sky above Ducheng;
The mountains and rivers of ten thousand ages are present before one's eyes. One must believe that the 'Dead Heart' does not die at all;
Last night, the autumn moon was once again full together with it."
Zhou Dunyi of Zhoulaocixi, courtesy name Maoshu, was a native of Chengleng. Having traveled to Mount Lu and taken delight in its secluded beauty, he subsequently built a residence there.
At that time, Foyin was residing at Luanxi; the Master visited him, and they discussed the Way together. [Foyin] asked: "That which is called the mandate of Heaven—"
"Nature. To follow one's nature is called the Way. [The official asked: "In the Chan school, why is it said that 'no-mind' is the Way?
The Master said: "If you have doubts, seek another teacher. The official said: "Seeking another is not impossible; but ultimately, what constitutes the Way? The Master said:

"The green mountains fill the eyes—look as you please. The official attained realization. One day, suddenly seeing weeds growing before his window, he said: "This is identical to my own inner state..."
Ban presented a verse to the Master, saying: "Originally there was no delusion in the past, and now there is no awakening; mind and object merge, revealing what was hidden in the depths.
Grass grows deep outside the window, and pines stand by the path; all day long they cause people to look upon them without weariness.

He then requested that the Master become the presiding master of the "Green Pines Society" (Qing Song She), drawing a parallel to the precedent of the "White Lotus Society" (Bai Lian She). Regarding Zhou Dunyi’s (Mao Shu) *Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate* (*Taiji tu*), its source traces back to Chen Tuan. Chen Tuan—

The Master [Zhang] wore hempen clothing (*māyī*). This is now precisely the method for transforming the mind. It is the transmission of the Master Yá of Māyī; the Master Zǒng of Dōnglín expanded upon it.
Among the disciples of Master Zǒng, Hóngyì wrote a book stating: "The study of *xìnglǐ* (the principles of human nature) truly originated with the two masters Yá and Zǒng of Dōnglín.
